instructions: Dice the 2 zucchini into 1/4-inch pieces. Mince the shallots. Grate the Parmesan.
Heat a 10-inch nonstick skillet with a lid over medium. Add the oil and the shallots and cook for 2 minutes, until soft.
Add the zucchini and 1/4 tsp of the salt. Cook, stirring now and then, for 5 minutes, until just tender. Transfer it into a large bowl and let it cool for 3 minutes.
In another bowl, whisk the 8 eggs with the milk, the remaining 1/2 tsp of salt and the pepper. Stir in the Parmesan.
Pour the eggs over the zucchini and stir. This is off the heat, so the eggs don't scramble.
Put the same skillet back over medium-low and melt the butter, swirling it to coat the bottom. Pour in the egg mixture.
Cover and cook for 10 to 12 minutes, until the edges are set and the center barely jiggles when you shake the pan.
Run a spatula around the edge. Slide the frittata onto a cutting board and cut it into wedges.
Taste a wedge. If it's flat, add a pinch more salt.
Serve warm or at room temperature. Leftovers keep in the fridge for 3 days and are good cold.
method_notes: No frittata di zucchine page had a usable star rating, so this leads with Food Network's version from Debi Mazar and Gabriele Corcos (unrated): shallot and diced zucchini in olive oil, eggs beaten with a little milk and Parmesan, then cooked covered in butter over medium-low heat. Food.com's Frittata Di Zucchine has 25 reviews but shows no average, Memorie di Angelina bakes it with fried zucchini rounds and Parmesan, and Nourish Evolution adds sweet onion and finishes under the broiler. This follows the lead, scaled from 6 to 8 eggs and from 1 to 2 zucchini so it feeds four as a dinner.
